status: Exploratory audit added after all 400 posts were collected and inspected.
limitations: No human preference, authorship detection, quality score or paid model judge. Overlapping criteria must not be summed as defects. All examples in this catalogue are authored illustrations.

sources.title: Notebook 15: What changes an AI judge's writing score?
sources.finding: Supplies eight context-sensitive prose criteria. A correctly quoted flag is not proof that its criticism is justified.

sources.title: Notebook 17: Writing validation
sources.locator: README, sections 7 and 10; neutral prose criteria
sources.finding: Fresh judges gave prose concerns on only 1.6% of opinions on previously flagged passages. Preserve the distinction between a surface match and a justified criticism.

sources.title: Why Does ChatGPT "Delve" So Much?
sources.finding: Identifies 21 exact word forms in scientific abstracts. These are historical vocabulary candidates, not a LinkedIn blacklist.

sources.title: Delving into LLM-assisted writing in biomedical publications through excess vocabulary
sources.finding: Motivates corpus frequency comparison. An individual word does not establish authorship or poor quality.

sources.title: Do LLMs write like humans? Variation in grammatical and rhetorical styles
sources.locator: Results on participial clauses, nominalization and coordination
sources.finding: Finds grammatical differences in GPT-4o and Llama 3 writing. Our small surface rules do not reproduce its linguistic parser.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Signs of AI writing
sources.finding: Suggests reviewing grand claims, forced contrasts, unnamed authorities and formulaic endings. Wikipedia genre conventions do not automatically transfer to LinkedIn.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Signs of AI writing/Style
sources.locator: Boldface; inline-header lists; title case; emoji
sources.finding: Suggests layout candidates. Presence alone does not measure excessive formatting.

sources.title: Anti-AI Writing Guide, Tundra AI Labs
sources.locator: Rhythm; contrasts; word choice; openers and closers
sources.finding: Offers editing preferences about clipped rhythm, rhetorical staging and generic benefits. Use as candidate generation, not measured prevalence.

sources.title: Claudisms
sources.finding: Provides additional candidate phrases. The site name does not establish that a phrase is specific to Claude.

sources.title: How To Write Without Sounding Like AI, George Kao
sources.finding: Recommends reviewing repeated sentence lengths and paragraph templates. These are preferences, not evidence about the four tested models.

sources.title: Fixing AI LinkedIn Posts That Scream ChatGPT, Iris Vandermeer
sources.locator: June 25, 2026, updated July 18; one-line paragraphs and closing questions
sources.finding: Suggests inspecting post shape and generic engagement requests. Its claims about training data and reader penalties are not adopted here.

styles.name: Vague abstraction
styles.definition: An abstract claim omits the actor, action or comparison a reader needs.
styles.explanation: The sentence sounds purposeful while leaving the practical change unclear.
styles.illustrative_example: This creates a new paradigm for enterprise value.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The tool checks invoices against purchase orders before payment.
styles.useful_when: An abstract summary can help after the concrete mechanism is explained.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Unnecessary jargon
styles.definition: Specialist or corporate wording adds decoding work without needed precision.
styles.explanation: Readers must translate the terminology before they can judge the claim.
styles.illustrative_example: Operationalize a synergistic inference enablement layer.
styles.clearer_rewrite: Let the support team run the model inside its ticketing system.
styles.useful_when: A technical term is useful when the audience needs its exact meaning.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Empty emphasis
styles.definition: Importance, novelty or certainty is asserted without supporting evidence.
styles.explanation: The adjective supplies enthusiasm in place of a checkable comparison.
styles.illustrative_example: An incredibly revolutionary breakthrough for every business.
styles.clearer_rewrite: In the reported test, median response time fell from four seconds to two.
styles.useful_when: A strong claim can be justified by a named comparison and evidence.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Repeated conclusion
styles.definition: A point is restated without new evidence or a useful role in the format.
styles.explanation: The reader spends time rereading a proposition instead of learning its implication.
styles.illustrative_example: The service costs less. In short, it is cheaper. The takeaway is lower cost.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The service costs less, but the quoted price excludes storage.
styles.useful_when: A summary can help in a long report, a slide deck or an accessibility context.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Padded construction
styles.definition: Extra scaffolding delays a proposition that could be stated directly.
styles.explanation: The sentence spends words announcing its job before doing it.
styles.illustrative_example: It is important to note that there is a need for an evaluation of the results.
styles.clearer_rewrite: Evaluate the results.
styles.useful_when: Framing may be needed to distinguish a recommendation from an observed fact.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Formulaic framing
styles.definition: A stock opener, contrast or slogan contributes little to this particular point.
styles.explanation: The same frame can surround unrelated news without changing its wording.
styles.illustrative_example: The future is here, and the possibilities are endless.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The release adds offline transcription in six languages.
styles.useful_when: A familiar structure can orient readers if the content makes it specific.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Stacked hedges
styles.definition: Several uncertainty markers qualify the same claim redundantly.
styles.explanation: The reader cannot tell whether the doubt comes from weak evidence or verbal caution.
styles.illustrative_example: This may potentially perhaps reduce errors.
styles.clearer_rewrite: It may reduce errors; the company has not published a controlled test.
styles.useful_when: Different qualifiers can express different uncertainties, so inspect their scope.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Unclear reference
styles.definition: The reader cannot recover an actor, pronoun, comparison or logical link.
styles.explanation: A grammatical sentence can still leave the reader unsure what caused what.
styles.illustrative_example: The vendor told the customer its model failed, which changed their plan.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The vendor said its own model failed. The customer then delayed deployment.
styles.useful_when: A pronoun is concise when its referent is clear from the surrounding text.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Repeated prestige vocabulary
styles.definition: A small vocabulary of impressive-sounding words recurs across unrelated subjects.
styles.explanation: Repeated diction can make separate posts sound interchangeable. Frequency alone is not a fault.
styles.illustrative_example: Delve into this intricate tapestry of transformative innovation.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The article explains how the new search index handles updates.
styles.useful_when: Literal or precise use is fine. A model habit requires counts across several topics.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Unnecessary negative contrast
styles.definition: A claim is framed by denying an alternative that the reader may never have proposed.
styles.explanation: The denial adds a dramatic turn and may set up a false choice.
styles.illustrative_example: This isn't a product launch. It's a revolution.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The launch adds a model marketplace to the existing product.
styles.useful_when: A contrast is useful when correcting an actual misunderstanding.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Automatic not-just expansion
styles.definition: A simple additional fact is presented as a correction or escalation.
styles.explanation: Repeated expansion makes ordinary additions sound like revelations.
styles.illustrative_example: It doesn't just summarize meetings; it transforms collaboration.
styles.clearer_rewrite: It summarizes meetings and assigns action items to attendees.
styles.useful_when: The form can clarify a real limitation in what readers already expect.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Mechanical groups of three
styles.definition: Lists or parallel phrases repeatedly use three items regardless of the evidence.
styles.explanation: A pleasing rhythm can encourage generic additions that do not add information.
styles.illustrative_example: Smarter. Faster. Better.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The reported test completed in two seconds and used half as much memory.
styles.useful_when: Three real findings deserve three items. A triad count cannot decide usefulness.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Trailing significance clause
styles.definition: A sentence ends with a participle that announces the importance of the preceding fact.
styles.explanation: The tail can substitute an interpretation for evidence supporting that interpretation.
styles.illustrative_example: The company added a dashboard, underscoring its commitment to innovation.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The company added a dashboard showing request costs by team.
styles.useful_when: A trailing clause is useful when it states a specific, supported consequence.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Inflated forms of is or has
styles.definition: A plain relation is replaced by a ceremonial verb phrase.
styles.explanation: The additional wording can imply significance that the relation itself does not carry.
styles.illustrative_example: The release stands as a testament to the team's vision.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The release includes the first version of the team's speech model.
styles.useful_when: Serves as is accurate when something has a particular function or role.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Question-and-answer pivot
styles.definition: The writer asks a short question and immediately supplies the answer.
styles.explanation: Used repeatedly, the device manufactures suspense and interrupts the argument.
styles.illustrative_example: The catch? You still need to check the output.
styles.clearer_rewrite: You still need to check the output.
styles.useful_when: A question can help when it is the reader's real question and needs explanation.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Throat clearing and signposting
styles.definition: Text announces the next statement instead of stating it.
styles.explanation: The opening or transition becomes longer without adding the promised content.
styles.illustrative_example: It's worth noting that the model runs locally.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The model runs locally.
styles.useful_when: Signposts help in a long document when they identify a meaningful change of topic.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Vague attribution
styles.definition: An opinion or finding is assigned to unnamed authorities.
styles.explanation: The reader cannot check the evidence or distinguish consensus from one opinion.
styles.illustrative_example: Experts agree that AI agents will replace most software.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The article quotes one analyst who expects agents to change software purchasing.
styles.useful_when: A collective attribution is useful when its membership and evidence are supplied.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Generic scene-setting opener
styles.definition: The first sentence describes a broad era or trend rather than this event.
styles.explanation: Many unrelated posts could begin with the same line, delaying the news.
styles.illustrative_example: In today's rapidly evolving digital world, innovation never stops.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The lab released its speech model on Tuesday.
styles.useful_when: Background can be needed when the intended reader does not know the subject.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Generic engagement close
styles.definition: A post ends by soliciting reactions without a specific question grounded in its argument.
styles.explanation: The request can feel attached to the post solely to collect comments.
styles.illustrative_example: Thoughts? Agree or disagree? Let me know below.
styles.clearer_rewrite: Which of these checks would your team require before giving an agent payment access?
styles.useful_when: A focused question can invite useful knowledge that the article does not answer.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Formulaic challenges and future ending
styles.definition: An ending acknowledges obstacles, then predicts a promising future without specifying either.
styles.explanation: The apparent balance can leave the reader without a decision or unresolved question.
styles.illustrative_example: Despite the challenges, the future looks bright as innovation continues.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The service still lacks an audit log; the vendor has not announced a release date.
styles.useful_when: Concrete limitations and dated plans are useful, even when placed at the end.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Announcing honesty
styles.definition: The writer labels a statement as honest, candid or real rather than supporting it.
styles.explanation: A sincerity cue can become a repeated substitute for explaining the evidence.
styles.illustrative_example: Let's be honest: this changes everything.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The price change would cut this example workload's bill from $40 to $25.
styles.useful_when: A candid statement can be appropriate in a personal account; the cue is not proof of insincerity.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Demonstrative payoff sentence
styles.definition: A paragraph ends with a short this or that sentence that labels its significance.
styles.explanation: Repeated payoffs can make the conclusion sound prewritten.
styles.illustrative_example: That's the unlock.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The change lets customers export their logs without a support request.
styles.useful_when: A short reference can tie together a genuinely complex preceding explanation.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Presupposed objection
styles.definition: The writer introduces an imagined reader objection and immediately defeats it.
styles.explanation: It can make an unsupported assumption about what the reader believes.
styles.illustrative_example: You might think this is just another chatbot, but hear me out.
styles.clearer_rewrite: Unlike the previous version, this system can schedule a meeting after confirmation.
styles.useful_when: Address an objection when readers have actually raised it or the evidence warrants it.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Unexplained analyst metaphor
styles.definition: A figurative word makes a point sound structural, hidden or profound without clarifying it.
styles.explanation: The metaphor can replace the mechanism the reader needs to understand.
styles.illustrative_example: This is the load-bearing shift quietly rewriting the physics of work.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The update lets the agent approve refunds up to a preset limit.
styles.useful_when: Literal uses and metaphors with a precise, explained mapping can help.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Staged reflection or discovery
styles.definition: The writer narrates an insight as a thought that keeps returning or an unexpected discovery.
styles.explanation: The autobiographical frame can add drama without adding evidence.
styles.illustrative_example: The question I keep coming back to changed how I see everything.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The unresolved question is who is liable when the agent issues a refund.
styles.useful_when: A true account of reflection is appropriate when the author supplies it.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Decorative or false range
styles.definition: A from-to construction implies a useful spectrum whose endpoints may not share one scale.
styles.explanation: The wording suggests breadth while obscuring which cases are actually covered.
styles.illustrative_example: From productivity to possibility, the platform does it all.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The platform transcribes calls and drafts follow-up emails.
styles.useful_when: A real range, such as prices from $5 to $20, is informative.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Noun-heavy wording
styles.definition: Actions are packaged as abstract nouns, sometimes hiding who acts.
styles.explanation: A dense string of process nouns makes the reader reconstruct the actors and verbs.
styles.illustrative_example: The implementation of the evaluation of deployment readiness is required.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The team must check whether the model is ready to deploy.
styles.useful_when: Terms such as calibration name useful concepts. A noun suffix does not establish a noun or a defect.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Repeated participial clauses
styles.definition: Sentences repeatedly add -ing clauses to compress actions or descriptions.
styles.explanation: Compression can blur timing, actors or causation. This is broader than a significance tail.
styles.illustrative_example: The agent reads the ticket, generating a reply, routing the case, reducing effort.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The agent reads the ticket and drafts a reply. A person decides where to route it.
styles.useful_when: A participial clause is useful when the actor and relationship are clear.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Repeated clipped rhythm
styles.definition: Several short sentences or fragments appear consecutively for emphasis.
styles.explanation: A constant staccato rhythm can make ordinary details sound artificially dramatic.
styles.illustrative_example: No forms. No friction. Just results.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The tool fills in the form using the customer record.
styles.useful_when: One short sentence can emphasize an important fact; fragments can suit some voices.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Repeated bold emphasis
styles.definition: A post repeatedly applies bold markers to selected phrases.
styles.explanation: When many phrases compete for emphasis, it becomes harder to see the main point.
styles.illustrative_example: **This launch** changes **everything** about **how we work**.
styles.clearer_rewrite: This launch adds two features: local search and a shared audit log.
styles.useful_when: A heading or one key figure can benefit from emphasis. LinkedIn may display literal Markdown markers.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Bold labels on every list item
styles.definition: List entries repeatedly begin with a bold label and a colon.
styles.explanation: A template can impose categories that do not help explain the substance.
styles.illustrative_example:
- **Impact:** A big change.
- **Future:** More innovation.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The price falls by 20%. The free tier still excludes private data.
styles.useful_when: Consistent labels are useful when comparing genuinely parallel attributes.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Emoji as repeated layout markers
styles.definition: Emoji introduce many lines, headings or bullet-like statements.
styles.explanation: Decoration can become the organizing device even when ordinary structure would be clearer.
styles.illustrative_example:
🚀 Big launch
💡 Huge insight
🔥 Massive opportunity
styles.clearer_rewrite: The release adds shared workspaces and a usage dashboard.
styles.useful_when: Emoji may fit an author's voice or aid scanning. Their presence is not inherently poor writing.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Title case and heading templates
styles.definition: Short posts use formal, capitalized section headings or repeat the same heading scheme.
styles.explanation: The post can read like an outline rather than a developed point.
styles.illustrative_example: ## The Future Of Intelligent Enterprise Transformation
styles.clearer_rewrite: What changes for support teams
styles.useful_when: Headings help in long or complex posts and may follow a publication's house style.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Mechanical one-sentence paragraphs
styles.definition: Most paragraphs contain one sentence, repeatedly separated by blank lines.
styles.explanation: Every sentence gets similar visual weight, which can interrupt connected reasoning.
styles.illustrative_example:
The model is faster.

The price is lower.

The stakes are high.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The model is faster and costs less, but the article does not test its error rate.
styles.useful_when: Short paragraphs can improve mobile reading. Density and runs are descriptive, not quality thresholds.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Chatbot or markup residue
styles.definition: The response includes assistant-facing commentary, placeholders or formatting artifacts instead of only the finished post.
styles.explanation: The draft can require cleanup or accidentally publish process instructions.
styles.illustrative_example: Certainly! Here is your post: [Insert personal story here].
styles.clearer_rewrite: Start with the supported news; add a personal story only when the author provides one.
styles.useful_when: An explicit placeholder may be useful in a requested template, and an editorial note can prevent an error.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Unsupported first-person experience
styles.definition: The draft gives the poster a personal experience, observation or emotion that the supplied material does not establish.
styles.explanation: A ready-to-publish draft may put an invented claim in the author's voice.
styles.illustrative_example: I spent last week testing this system with my team.
styles.clearer_rewrite: The article reports a week-long test by the vendor's team.
styles.useful_when: First-person judgment is different from biography. An author-supplied experience is valid.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Generic benefit language
styles.definition: A product benefit is described without saying what task changes or for whom.
styles.explanation: Readers cannot connect the promise to a concrete use or limitation.
styles.illustrative_example: It does the heavy lifting so you can focus on what matters.
styles.clearer_rewrite: It matches receipts to card transactions; you review unmatched items.
styles.useful_when: A short slogan can accompany a specific explanation, especially in advertising.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Uniform sentence and paragraph rhythm
styles.definition: Successive sentences or paragraphs repeatedly have the same length or internal template.
styles.explanation: A predictable cadence can make distinct points feel interchangeable. There is no universal ideal length.
styles.illustrative_example: A post gives every point one claim, one example and one recap, even when the example adds nothing.
styles.clearer_rewrite: Give a complex point the explanation it needs; let a simple fact occupy one sentence.
styles.useful_when: Parallel structure can help readers compare genuinely similar cases.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Repeated punctuation for emphasis
styles.definition: One punctuation device repeatedly supplies pauses, suspense or excitement.
styles.explanation: Habitual dashes, ellipses or exclamation marks can give every sentence the same emotional weight.
styles.illustrative_example: A new model! A new era! An entirely new way to work!
styles.clearer_rewrite: The model adds image input. The article does not report a comparison with the earlier version.
styles.useful_when: Punctuation can convey a real relationship or fit an author's voice. Count it without treating it as proof of AI authorship.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

styles.name: Automatic hashtag tail
styles.definition: Every post ends with a block of generic topic labels.
styles.explanation: The ending may look templated, especially when tags repeat across unrelated articles.
styles.illustrative_example: #AI #Innovation #FutureOfWork #Leadership
styles.clearer_rewrite: Use only tags that serve the intended audience, or end after the last useful sentence.
styles.useful_when: A relevant tag can help organize a series or address a particular community.
styles.example_kind: authored teaching example; not a measured response

entries.label: Canned insight cue
entries.regex: \b(?:the truth is|the reality is|at its core|what's interesting is|the bigger point is)\b
entries.definition: An introductory cue claims to reveal a truth, reality, essence or bigger point.
entries.illustrative_example: The reality is that the tool still needs approval.

entries.label: Honesty cue
entries.regex: \b(?:honestly|to be honest|let's be honest|real talk|i'll be straight with you|the honest (?:part|framing))\b
entries.definition: The writer explicitly labels the statement as honest or candid.
entries.illustrative_example: Let's be honest: the service is expensive.

entries.label: Rhetorical label
entries.regex: \b(?:worth naming|worth stating clearly|reality check|uncertainty flag|on the substance)\s*:
entries.definition: A colon-ended label announces the kind of statement about to follow.
entries.illustrative_example: Reality check: the test used only ten cases.

entries.label: Quietly or silently
entries.definition: The adverbs quietly and silently; literal and figurative uses are both counted.
entries.illustrative_example: The update is quietly changing the industry.

entries.label: Load-bearing
entries.definition: The literal expression load-bearing, with a space or hyphen; metaphor requires inspection.

entries.label: Does real work
entries.definition: A claim that a distinction or other subject does real work, without judging whether the work is explained.

entries.label: That's why / where / the
entries.definition: A this/that cue introduces a why/where explanation or labels an unlock, shift, point or lesson.

entries.label: Imagined objection cue
entries.regex: \b(?:you might think|you may think|hear me out|this (?:sounds|may sound))\b
entries.definition: A cue imagines what the reader thinks or asks them to hear the writer out; it may address a real objection.
entries.illustrative_example: You might think the test is complete.

entries.label: Less about / more about
entries.definition: A sentence contrasts less about one thing with more about another within a bounded span.
entries.illustrative_example: It is less about speed and more about cost.

entries.label: More than just
entries.definition: The exact expansion phrase more than just.
entries.illustrative_example: It is more than just a chatbot.

entries.label: Comma followed by not
entries.definition: A comma is followed by not and a short phrase; the negation may be useful or factually necessary.
entries.illustrative_example: It is a workflow, not a chatbot.

entries.label: Canned reassurance cue
entries.regex: \b(?:the good news is|you're not alone|don't worry|it doesn't have to be this way)\b
entries.definition: A familiar transition reassures the reader or announces good news.
entries.illustrative_example: The good news is that access is free.

entries.label: Is key / crucial / essential
entries.definition: An is/are statement calls its subject key, crucial or essential.

entries.label: Generic benefit phrase
entries.regex: \b(?:do(?:es|ing)? the heavy lifting|focus on what matters|without lifting a finger|without missing a beat|(?:reduce|reduces|reducing) friction|(?:create|creates|creating) clarity|(?:build|builds|building) momentum|(?:drive|drives|driving) alignment)\b
entries.definition: A benefit is expressed through a fixed effort, clarity, friction, momentum or alignment slogan.

entries.label: Reflective pose phrase
entries.definition: A fixed phrase frames a thought as worth contemplation or an idea the writer has arrived at.

entries.label: Coming back to
entries.definition: The writer describes returning to a thought; literal movement is also matched.
entries.illustrative_example: I keep coming back to this question.

entries.label: Recurring-question frame
entries.regex: \bthe question (?:that (?:kept|keeps) coming up|i keep coming back to)\b
entries.definition: A question is framed as repeatedly arising or occupying the writer.
entries.illustrative_example: The question I keep coming back to is cost.

entries.label: Discovery-arc cue
entries.regex: \b(?:i didn't (?:plan|set out)|what i didn't expect to find|the (?:thread|thing) i didn't plan)\b
entries.definition: A first-person setup says the writer did not plan, intend or expect the discovery.
entries.illustrative_example: I didn't set out to find this pattern.

entries.label: Personal peak cue
entries.regex: \b(?:the one that surprised me most|what struck me hardest|the part that stuck with me most|if i had to pick one)\b
entries.definition: A personal-superlative cue selects the most surprising or memorable item; a justified ranking is also matched.
entries.illustrative_example: The one that surprised me most was speed.

entries.label: Physics phrase
entries.definition: A fixed physics phrase; the rule cannot distinguish literal science from a grand metaphor.
entries.illustrative_example: It changes the physics of work.

entries.label: Lives in / at
entries.definition: The expression lives in or lives at; physical residence and abstract placement are both matched.
entries.illustrative_example: The risk lives in the workflow.

entries.label: Despite-challenges phrase
entries.definition: A bounded despite-these/the/its-challenges formula; a concrete obstacle can still be useful.
entries.illustrative_example: Despite these challenges, the future is bright.

entries.label: Future-outlook label
entries.definition: A future-outlook/prospects label or a claim that the future looks bright or promising.

entries.label: Broader trend cue
entries.regex: \b(?:reflects? broader|part of a broader|represents? a significant shift|marks? a (?:key|major) turning point)\b
entries.definition: A cue places an event in a broader movement or calls it a significant shift or turning point.
entries.illustrative_example: This is part of a broader movement.

entries.label: Vague-connection cue
entries.definition: An association is described as close, deep or strong; specificity must be checked in context.
entries.illustrative_example: The tool is closely linked to progress.

entries.label: Unnamed authority cue
entries.definition: A fixed expression invokes unnamed experts, observers or shared belief; a name elsewhere may resolve it.

entries.label: Tokens ending in -tion/-sion/-ment/-ness/-ity
entries.definition: Counts suffix-bearing tokens, including false positives; no part-of-speech tagging.

entries.label: Comma followed by an -ing word
entries.definition: Counts an immediately post-comma -ing word, not all participial clauses.
entries.illustrative_example: The model reads the ticket, generating a reply.

entries.label: Three short comma-separated spans
entries.definition: Matches three short lexical spans; does not establish three parallel grammatical items.
entries.illustrative_example: It is fast, reliable, and secure.

entries.label: From-to span
entries.definition: Finds a range-shaped span; real numeric and temporal ranges are also matched.
entries.illustrative_example: From productivity to possibility, it does it all.

entries.label: First-person experience cue
entries.definition: Finds a small set of first-person verbs; unsupported experience requires comparison with the article.
entries.illustrative_example: I spent last week testing the service.

entries.label: Ultimately / all in all
entries.definition: A conventional summary transition appears; whether it repeats a conclusion is not judged.

entries.label: Assistant residue cue
entries.regex: \b(?:here(?:'s| is) (?:your|a) (?:linkedin )?post|i hope (?:this|that) helps|as an ai|my knowledge cutoff)\b
entries.definition: A fixed assistant-facing introduction, helpfulness closing or AI/cutoff self-reference appears.

entries.label: Bold spans
entries.definition: Number of **...** or __...__ spans.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing

entries.label: Bold list labels
entries.definition: Lines with a list marker or emoji, then a bold label and a colon.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing

entries.label: Share of words inside bold spans
entries.definition: Bold-span words divided by all post words.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing

entries.label: Emoji-prefixed lines
entries.definition: Lines beginning with a code point in the documented emoji ranges.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing

entries.label: Markdown headings
entries.definition: Lines beginning with one to six # signs and a space.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing

entries.label: Title-case Markdown headings
entries.definition: Headings with at least three alphabetic words, all non-stopwords beginning uppercase.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing

entries.label: Exactly three-item list blocks
entries.definition: Contiguous marked list runs containing exactly three lines.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing

entries.label: One-sentence paragraph share
entries.definition: Share of substantive, non-list paragraphs split into one sentence.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing

entries.label: Runs of at least three one-sentence paragraphs
entries.definition: Maximal runs of at least three one-sentence substantive non-list paragraphs.
entries.illustrative_example:
A fact.

Another fact.

A third fact.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing

entries.label: Runs of at least three short sentences
entries.definition: Maximal runs of at least three consecutive sentences, each one to six words.
entries.illustrative_example: It is here. It is fast. It costs less.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing

entries.label: Horizontal rules
entries.definition: Lines containing at least three identical -, * or _ characters.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing

entries.label: Code fences
entries.definition: Lines beginning with three backticks.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing

entries.label: Placeholders
entries.definition: Bracketed insert/add/your-text placeholders.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing

entries.label: Em dashes
entries.definition: Literal em dash characters in the proposed post.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing

entries.label: Exclamation marks
entries.definition: Literal exclamation marks in the proposed post.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing

entries.label: Hashtags
entries.definition: Hash-prefixed word tokens; headings with # plus a space are excluded.
entries.interpretation: descriptive formatting; no threshold for bad writing
